completion_data.completion_summary: Added an optional, additive --phase-check=warn|refuse flag to update-task-status.sh that independently counts a task's plan-file phase headings and warns/refuses an implement postflight transition on conclusive evidence of incomplete phases; threaded refuse at the 3 zero-gate sites (reconcile-task-status.sh x2, command-gate-out.sh) and skill-implementer/-hard, and warn at the 3 orchestrate sites (via skill_postflight_update's new optional 5th arg) and the 4 lean/cslib extension implementers, after an empirical validation gate (10/10 sampled completed tasks all-COMPLETED) cleared refuse for rollout. No-flag default proven byte-for-byte unchanged across a 24-cell operation x target_status x task-state dry-run matrix.

memory_candidates.content: When a bash script must resolve its repo-root relative to a source-store deploy tree (e.g. .claude/scripts/ deployed from agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/), guard scripts against direct execution from the source store with a deploy-root-guard.sh check — running from the source store makes SCRIPT_DIR/../.. resolve to a bogus repo root, silently corrupting any relative path derivation. When live-testing such a script's behavior without a full deploy, temporarily copy the modified source file over the deployed copy (which is gitignored/disposable), run the test, then restore — this preserves correct PROJECT_ROOT resolution without violating a source-store-only edit constraint.

guard-destructive-git.sh's over-staging heuristic for 'git commit -a/-am' scans the entire commit command text (including multi-line -m message bodies, but only the first line since it's extracted via a single-line grep -oE) for a regex matching '-<letters>a<letters>' bounded by whitespace/start/end. Hyphenated compound words in a commit message's first line, like 'zero-gate' (the '-gate' suffix contains 'a' and looks like a flag), trigger a false positive BLOCKED error even though no -a flag was passed. Workaround: avoid hyphenated words in the first line of commit messages, or rephrase (e.g. 'zero-gate' -> 'zero gate').

For a phase-accounting or completion backstop that must add a hard REFUSE mode, gate the refuse rollout behind an empirical validation phase that samples real historical completed-task artifacts (e.g. plan files) and checks the assumed invariant (e.g. 'phase headings converge to COMPLETED on genuine completion') holds at a set threshold (e.g. >=80%) before wiring refuse anywhere. If the gate fails, downgrade every planned refuse site to warn-only and record the gap as a follow-up blocker rather than shipping an unverified hard-refusal path.
